speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: A young girl has been traumatised and a boy's life has ended prematurely.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We must do right by these two young lives.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is tragic that such an incident has taken place.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It has been a very trying and distressing period for both families.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are very aware of that and we have refrained from commenting in detail on the matter for two reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: One, out of respect for Benjamin's memory and to protect the young girl as well; and, two, because it would be improper to discuss the facts in detail − which will be disputed − prior to the Coroner's Inquiry (CI).

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Given that a CI is pending, I took advice from AGC on what I can say today.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They have advised that I can set out what I am going to in the speech.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But I do so with considerable reservations and I will explain later why.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I will now deal with the questions raised by Members by looking at the following: one, what are the facts in this case; two, what is the Police Protocol for interviewing young persons; three, the deliberate falsehoods that have been spread in this case to blemish the Police; some people were doing this, as I will show later; and four, why has my Ministry not commented in detail, until now, on the matter?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I want to emphasise that the facts are as we know them now, at this stage.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Whenever I refer to facts, that is the basis on which I refer to them.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There are two aspects to the facts in this case: one, why Benjamin was asked to assist the Police in the investigations; and two, how the Police investigated the case.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Amongst other things, Police retrieved the relevant CCTV footages.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: A boy in school uniform was identified as the suspect.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The boy was later identified as Benjamin Lim.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On that day, 25 January 2016, while he was coming home from school, it appears that he made a detour.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He went to another block in the neighbourhood, before going home.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He seemed to have followed the 11-year-old girl.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The two appear not to have met before.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: He went into a lift at her block, at the ground floor.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And he is said to have molested the girl in the lift.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There are CCTV footages showing Benjamin making his way to the other block, Benjamin quickly following the girl into the lift after she entered it and there is CCTV footage, within the lift, showing what happened.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The girl has said to the Police that Benjamin touched a part of her body.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: After the incident, he stepped out of the lift at the 13th floor.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The girl said there was a brief exchange between them when he stepped out of the lift.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: CCTV footage then shows Benjamin going down one floor to the 12th floor and then taking the lift down to the ground floor.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It would appear, therefore, that his purpose of him getting into the lift was to follow her and, after the incident, get out and go back.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The family filed a Police report on the same day, 25 January.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Now, let me turn to the Police investigations.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As stated earlier, Police retrieved some CCTV footages.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Based on his school uniform, Police identified the boy to be from North View Secondary School.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Five officers went: three from the Neighbourhood Police Centre (NPC) and two from Division.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The three NPC officers have detailed knowledge of the community, they interact with the schools, they interact with the community and the teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They link up with the school; they make interactions smooth; they answer questions that the school may have.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Divisional officers assist in the investigation of cases.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The five officers were not in Police uniforms.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They were not in any attire with the word "Police".

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They went in plain clothes, in unmarked cars.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The officers showed a screenshot of the CCTV footages to the school officials.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The boy in the screenshot was identified to be Benjamin Lim.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: A school official then brought Benjamin to the Principal's office.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The officer spoke with Benjamin about the incident.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The other four Police officers were not present.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: After the interview, Benjamin was advised to call his mother by the Principal.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Benjamin was then brought back to the station in an unmarked car with three officers.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: One of the officers alighted along the way.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That left two officers in the car: one to drive and the other to look after Benjamin.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: At Ang Mo Kio station, an officer recorded Benjamin's statement.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This was done by the officer at his workstation, in an open plan office.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The first page shows the overall layout of the office and the particular workstation where Benjamin was interviewed is circled.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The second page shows a specific photo of the workstation as well as the passageway in between the workstations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The third page shows a sketch of the specific workstation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: L1 is where the interviewing officer sat, L2 is where Benjamin sat, and L3, within the same cubicle was where another officer sat doing his own unrelated work.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The fourth page shows a photograph of the chairs in the cubicle in question.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As Members can see, Benjamin was interviewed in a typical open office setting and another officer unrelated to the case was nearby doing his own work.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There were other officers at their respective workstations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He requested to be given some time to collect his thoughts about the incident.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: His written statement was taken at a quarter past 12, after he said he was ready.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He was offered food and drinks after the interview and he declined that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: After the interview, he was placed in a Temporary Holding Room which was secured.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This was pending his mother taking him back.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police then recorded a statement from the mother who was at the station.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He left the Police station with his mother and sister.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Time spent by Benjamin in the Police station was about three and a half hours which included the time Police spent taking a statement from the mother.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That was the last contact between the Police and Benjamin.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What happened after Benjamin and his mother left the Police station?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Based on investigations, the following is what we know.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Sometime later, his mother told Benjamin that he would not be going to the school camp that was to start the next day.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That was after a telephone conversation between the mother and a school counsellor.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Minister of Education will provide more details on that conversation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Now, let us ask a question: if Benjamin had not taken his own life, what would have happened in this case?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Another 15% of the cases are under consideration.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Charges are usually only brought against young persons when there are aggravating factors, such as when the offence is of a serious nature like rioting, or if the young person is a repeat offender, or has breached the terms of a conditional warning, for example, by failing to complete the necessary Guidance Programme.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As the statistics show, the Police's approach to young persons is, wherever possible, to try and avoid criminalising the conduct.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He is unlikely to have been charged in Court.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police would have taken into account his age, the fact that this is the first time and while all molests are taken seriously, the nature of the specific molest in any case has to be considered.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The nature of the alleged molest in this particular case can be characterised as being less serious in a range.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I would, however, caution that the statistics I have given and the relatively tolerant approach that the Police take towards young persons should not be seen as a licence for young persons to commit offences on the basis that seven out of 10 will not be charged.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police Protocol for dealing with young persons.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police adopt an expedited process for young persons: to interview them and release them as quickly as possible to their parents.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Where suitable, a young person will be placed on a programme to help him.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The focus is on diversionary supervision and counselling.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police guidelines are for the school to be kept updated on the progress of the case.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That will allow the school to monitor and support the student.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One suggestion that has been made is to video-record interviews of all minors.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have announced last year that we are studying the matter of video recording.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will make further announcements when we have worked through the legal and other issues.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Another suggestion that has been made is that we extend the Appropriate Adult Scheme to all young persons being interviewed.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have the Appropriate Adult Scheme to provide assistance to suspects who have mental and intellectual disabilities.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The role of the Appropriate Adult is to assist these persons to communicate more effectively with the Police.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police have said in their statement of 1 February that they will consider this point during the review.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Association of Criminal Lawyers of Singapore (ACLS) has contacted us and offered to give us their views.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will engage them and get their views.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I will caution against rushing to conclusions at this stage.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If there is something we can do better, we will do so.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In the review, the following three broad points will be taken into account, in addition to other factors.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Those three points are: one, what happened in this case; two, the types of young persons who get picked up; and three, how can we reduce systemic risk.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Are there any specific indications in this case that the processes need to be changed?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have set out how the investigation was done.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Suicide often involves a very complex set of factors.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One has to look at the facts carefully, consult experts to try and get an assessment as to what happened.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police will also consult psychologists and other relevant experts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some people have asked: why did we need to take him out of the school?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Could we not have waited until Benjamin got home?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When Police went to the school, they did not know who he was or his history.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: An accused person unknown to the Police could well have engaged in other molest, and until then, maybe no one had reported.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the Police wait, and he molests someone else in the meantime, then the question would be: why did the Police not move in faster?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When an incident happens, as a general rule, I am sure we want the Police to move in quickly.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What do Members think the public's attitudes will be if it was the victim of the molest who had committed suicide?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police would be expected to have moved quickly.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This will become clearer when I deal with my next point: the types of young persons we pick up.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Young people get picked up for a wide range of offences, from rioting, sexual assault, physical assault to even murder.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police need to move quickly, arrest, investigate, before the others, including other gang members, destroy evidence.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Should we make distinctions based on the types of offences involved?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What about deliberate arson or Unlicensed Money Lending cases?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What about those which are more security related; say, a 14-year-old, who was radicalised and wants to go out and kill?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He had wanted to go and fight in the Middle East.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We cannot assume that all Police officers will always follow protocols.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There will be some who will be tempted to take shortcuts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have to ensure that we have a system that minimises the risks.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I say minimise, because there is no system in the world that I know of which eliminates the risks completely.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This factor of needing to minimise the risk will be taken into account when we review the Protocol.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In this context, Police will look at past experience, the thousands of young persons who have been investigated.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Members can see that there are many aspects to this issue, many questions which need to be carefully considered.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The current Protocol had considered these, but we will review again.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is not a situation where we should have knee-jerk reactions or come to hasty conclusions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Any of our children could have been in Benjamin's position and any of our daughters could have been in that 11-year-old girl's position.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will approach the review of the processes with that perspective.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: My Ministry has the responsibility for the Protocol that is in place.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And ultimately, responsibility is with me, as the Minister.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Their responsibility is to act according to the Protocol in place.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If there are questions about the Protocols, I will answer, as I am doing now.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If there are issues with the Protocol, the responsibility is mine.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Let us not attack the Police officers who cannot defend themselves.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They are doing their job every day in difficult circumstances.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is the third of my four major points.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There have been a number of inaccurate statements that have been put out.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We say "inaccurate", based on the facts the Police have.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: A number of these falsehoods have been put out by The Online Citizen (TOC).

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It has gone on a planned, orchestrated campaign, using falsehoods and has published about 20 articles or so, as part of its campaign.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One example of the falsehoods, as I had said earlier, Police have said on 1 February that they went down in plain clothes, yet TOC published an article on 5 February saying that Police wore attire stating the word "Police".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The suggestion is that the Police were lying to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They supposedly relied on a posting by a lady, Mary Anne Pereira.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: She had stated that her son saw Police officers in Polo T-shirts with the word "Police".

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: She is wrong because the Police went to the school in plain clothes on 26 January.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is why there is a Court process to establish the truth.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is sad to see this level of dishonesty and politicisation of this matter.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Where the Police are wrong, we must and we will take action.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But we should not allow deliberate, dishonest attacks.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have asked my Ministry to study how the Police and other institutions can respond in future to such falsehoods.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Many of them are honest, reasonable people, who have genuine questions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But as I read the commentaries, it seems that many based themselves on a misperception of the facts which I had referred to earlier.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is the right forum for the relevant facts to be dealt with.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think Members will know when I keep quiet, usually there is a good reason; a good legal reason.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They issued a statement, an open letter, signed by Benjamin's father.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That statement contradicted some of the things Police had said on 1 February and made some additional points which the Police disagreed with.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The family also suggested that Benjamin had been coerced into admitting to the molest.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police could have immediately rebutted the family's statement.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police could have set out their version, like what I have set out today.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police could have released the CCTV footages, which would show, quite objectively, what happened inside the lift.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They could have referred to the open plan office; they could have referred to him making a detour from school to home and going into the lift with the girl.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They could have shown that he went up; the incident took place; he then got out and ran back down.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But is that the right thing to do?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: To have a public trial by media, at this stage; rebut the family in public and add to the family's grief?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The answer, in good sense, is clearly no.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We can understand that the family, in their grief, may genuinely believe some things, and, perhaps, even assert them in public.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police have also continued to engage the family.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When Police spoke with Benjamin's family last week, his father told us that the family felt pressured by the public and media attention.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Photographers and reporters have been loitering around their house.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He asked for privacy and explained that he would like his family to be kept out of the spotlight.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He asked that we inform the media of this and tell the media that the family did not want their identity, names, pictures published.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Ultimately, it will be up to the Court to decide.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Yesterday, the father spoke with a Police officer.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Now, let me deal with the second reason why we did not comment in detail, until today.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The CI will, to the extent possible, try to establish the cause of Benjamin's death and the facts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For example in this case, it can be argued that the identity of the 11-year-old girl should not be revealed.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: She is a young victim who has been deeply traumatised, and it could be argued that the CCTV footage of what happened within the lift should be viewed in private as well, for the sake of Benjamin's memory and for the young girl.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Once the Coroner announces his findings, both facts and conclusions, then people can offer their criticisms, viewpoints, comments on what the Police did, what my Ministry did, or did not do.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is the official version of the facts, after people are cross-examined on the stand.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Sub judice principles set out what can and cannot be said when a Court hearing or Inquiry is pending.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Coroner decides on the scope of the Inquiry based on the Coroner's Act.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some of these issues may be raised at, or become relevant, at the Inquiry.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Police came out publicly on 1 February – six days after the incident, five days after they went to the school – to say there would be a Coroner's Inquiry once Police investigations into the death were completed.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And Police said in their statement that all relevant facts would be presented, and where the family would be able to raise all questions that they may have.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There is no such thing as a cover-up.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Yet, some, like TOC, continued making accusations, insinuations, speculating on the facts, well after that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As I have said, it is understandable when the family said some things.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But TOC and its ilk should not engage in this, prior to the Coroner's Inquiry.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They tried to get the Police to comment on allegations relating to this case and further assert that since the Police and the Ministry were not responding, therefore, the Police must be guilty of the various allegations, assertions that have been made.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is surprising that even a lawyer, Mr Thio Shen Yi, has made some comments which should never have been made.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He has said five Police officers spoke to Benjamin.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He has said that five officers took Benjamin to the Police station, that is also false; and that Police should have behaved in a less intimidating way.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He seems to make the assertion of intimidation, based on his other statements which are themselves false.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: His statements practically imply that Benjamin killed himself because of police intimidation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr Thio has a duty to be fair to the Police officers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He need only to have referred to the Police statement of 1 February to know that many of the assertions he is making are untrue.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And without knowing anything about Benjamin, his mental make-up, his family background, one cannot reach such conclusions that he was intimidated and that is why he took his life.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: A lawyer should know that it would be useful to get some expert evidence.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: My officials and I personally have spoken with the former Chief Psychologist of IMH, Prof Long.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: He told us you look at the following things amongst others.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: People sometimes take their lives when they reach a point of hopelessness; they give up on life.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What were the possible reasons Benjamin gave up on his life?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This may involve having to look at, one, his mental state before the incident – depends on a variety of factors, surrounding circumstances and the time period could stretch some way back, even years.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One has to also consider what were the stressors in Benjamin's life before the incident.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What led him to engage in this incident?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the behaviour was not normal, what was going on in his mind?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Two, you look at the events on the day, including his conduct during the incident and the interview.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And, three, the events after the interview, including his various interactions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, there were many aspects to look at and it would not be accurate at all at this stage to fix on any one particular point and say with certainty that that was the reason why the suicide took place.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr Thio and others have also referred to other issues, early access to counsel being one of them.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On early access to counsel, there are reasonable arguments both ways.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Our position on early access to counsel has been made clear previously.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We had arrived at this position after thoroughly considering the matter and taking into account all the relevant factors.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am prepared to explain again our reasons and thinking behind this position in due course at a more appropriate time.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Today, I would like to keep discussions to this case.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Next, let me say about the discussions today.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Amongst other things, public confidence in the Police Force must be maintained.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have myself commented on some occasions in the past, when a case is pending.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When I have done so, I had carefully considered the legal position and kept within the principles of sub judice.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: TOC and some others have ignored the pending Coroner's Inquiry and have made wild allegations in this matter.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is in the public interest that we clarify the position.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As to what happens to the people who have made those allegations, I will prefer not to comment today.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As we go forward, from time to time, there will be other incidents in the future.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We must have a clear proper framework to deal with them, such that when an incident happens, first the facts have to be established.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We must also avoid attacking institutions and individuals based on those hasty conclusions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We must allow the facts to be established first.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There are proper processes for all facts to come out.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Second, if there are going to be public hearings, we should not prejudice or prejudge the hearings.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There can be a full, open discussion, once the hearings are over.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think Members will agree that the facts that I have set out should ideally be first dealt with at a proper inquiry and people must have the ability to test those facts, and police officers may have to be cross-examined.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Judge will make the finding and then we can discuss.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And with your permission, Mdm Speaker, in the interest of clarity and expedience, may I request that Members raise clarifications relating to my Statement first, followed by those relating to Minister Ng's Statement.
